1-bora-adamantaneamine derivatives have a selective astrocyte antiproliferate effect that can be used as a novel class of anti-HCV agents with the potential to bind to and activate CD81.
the 1-boradamantaneamines and related analogues are promising leads for the development of novel anti-HCV agents that bind and activate CD81.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have synthesized a library of over five hundred compounds and have identified a class of amine complexes of 1-boradamantane that selectively bind CD81 and have a dose-dependent antiprolferative effect on CD 81-enriched cells (astrocytes) vs CD81-depleted cells (C6 gliomas) at concentrations of 0.1 to 10 micromolar.
the amine complexes of 1-boradamantane have the potential to bind to the CD81 tetraspanin protein.
the 1-boradamantaneamine amantidine analogs display a dose-dependent, selective astrocyte antiproliferate effect relative to C6 glioma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
1-bora-adamataneamine derivatives have the ability to bind CD81 with a higher affinity and selectivity than amantidine.

we were able to synthesize a library of over one thousand compounds and screen them for astrocyte-selectivity in a CD81-dependent manner, with the goal of identifying compounds that could be used as potential anti-hepatitis-C agents.

1-bora-2-adamantylamine and its amide derivatives display a significant antiviral effect on CD81-expressing astrocytes vs CD81-defective C6 glioma cells, and this antiviral effect appears to be CD81-dependent.
